'under payment-by-weight, none of what follows would have cost anyone a dollar'

Ostrey Hollow station, seven miles up-valley, winter 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896, glass borrowed from Larrow Green
No account anywhere in Section A of the bench system: no weighing at intake, no composite sample, no percent scale on the bottle neck for a fixed pipette charge, no skim returned

Story 3: 'not seasonally, but flat, year-round, in every month alike', 0.19 constant

Ansel Keddie b.1861, 29 seasons from the 1896 opening, dismissed 30 April 1925, died Feb 1934
Test book kept in Keddie's own hand from 1896, entries within 0.03, tested 31x weekly for 29 seasons
Summary leaf: 3.61 from 1898 given, but the 1896 figure of 3.80 on borrowed glass never appears in Section A; both figures required
8 May to 10 July 1911, nine weeks, borrowed measure, question mark — core of the item present (the 3.80 level is not, but four elements are bolded and the core is intact)

1919 circular present, but Keddie's 17 March 1925 statement ('tested as he was taught, cannot say why') is nowhere in the answers
Died 1934 still under the imputation; book impounded 1925, to the county historical rooms 1959
Six farms on Hessel Bottom (Story 6), Emmet Brant the largest patron (Story 3)
Weigh book from 1 January 1897 and the two scales always agreed

1902 complaints present, but Story 3 states the Hollow-vs-Larrow-Green comparison (3.61 vs 3.78) as 'a constant deficiency of 0.19 points' and treats Roy Brant's 'seventeen hundredths' as merely 'close' — exactly the conflation of the two gaps the key charges for

To Roy in 1929, lent to Ivy in 1958, to Hazel at Roy's death in 1962

From 1915, four of the six farms hauled over in the summer flush, station the rest of the year

Explicitly kills both watering and wet hay: same hay and herds measured elsewhere tested normally

Condemnation on 12 June 1923 correctly dated in Story 7 (burette check not stated, but the core is present)

Replacement glass 28 June / 2 July 1923 appears only in Section E; the 1924 average of 3.80 and the fact that nobody connected the rise with the condemnation are absent from Section A
Crate to the loft; notebooks to the state office 1936, Farland library 1947, where Ivy found the 1923 volume
Patrons' petition of January 1925 stated twice
Frick's board, 17 March - 4 May 1925, three sessions, two in the station weigh room
Water (Vose), tester theft (Teague), wet hay (1908 report) all three argued; board 'found no cause established'
Four books: station test book, receiving book, Brant's weigh book, the 1923 inspector's notebook
Dismissal 30 April 1925 four days before an award finding nothing; $3,800 'without admission' on 4 May

Ivy Keddie, granddaughter, graduate student at the State Agricultural College at Farland, Vaught named

February 1958, crate in the station loft, nine surviving pipettes
9 March 1958, calibrated burette, 16.72 against a marked 17.6, ~5% short / 95% of true
95 percent of true for as long as the glass was in service (1 May 1897 to 12 June 1923), 3.61 against 3.80, 0.19, explicitly proportional not additive

Bulletin No. 471, October 1958, clearing him twenty-four years after his death
Granddaughter

Second cousins with the full derivation through Orra and Emmet

Gideon Vose, father; nephew rumor rejected with two independent denials

$77.93, with $77.39 identified as the transposition
6 dozen = 72, each short 0.88 c.c.

A02 correctly abstained: reports both memories and says the 1896 intake cannot be determined
The pipette named as the single changed variable
Tester, herds, pasture, season, oversight held constant

Both halves: cause in the instrument rather than milk, cows, feed or honesty; and the limits (no magnitude, borrowed measure not proved accurate)
Ledger surplus (r05/r12), Alder Corners (r10), 1911 interval (r03/r18) — three sourced reasons from three narrators
States the three trails are unconnected and that (1) and (2) hold without the 1958 measurement

Answers yes, he knew; the 1919 circular over his own signature is cited at B3

A03 asserted: 'Vose was aware, at least from 1916, that the ledger showed something that needed explaining, and chose not to pursue it' — precisely the station-gain-told-him/let-it-run assertion the key penalizes (-2)

Capped at 3; a dedicated shared-wrong-value section with breakers: $3,500 (r01/r21), 44M and 3.16 cluster, eleven pipettes (r12/r19), 'two tenths' (r15/r16), five dozen (r11/r21), plus 16.27 (r11/r19) and 12 July (r08/r12)
A10 earned (by-law year undeterminable, lost minute book). A04 not abstained — the reground-mold accident is adopted. A06 never raised
Explicit self-contradiction list: r07's catalogue vs its own transcription, r11's Section V vs its conclusion, r15's letter vs its report, r22's correction, r12's retraction
1897 lot, 16.72 against 17.6, ~5 percent proportional not additive, 0.19 at the station's level, onset 1 May 1897 off borrowed glass, cessation 12 June 1923, nothing on the farms changing
Watering named (Vose, Sill) and defeated by Strawn's lactometer visits and sixteen years of clean Alder Corners cheese
Theft named (Toland, Teague) and defeated by cream arriving heavy in the accuser's own ledger, plus the 1911 interval
Bog hay named (Grigg's 1908 committee, Kepp) and defeated by Bulletin 214's actual 0.05 in winter and by Alder Corners
A07 asserted with a flat headline 'No.' — the board never examined the glassware. Assertion (-2)
A05 correctly abstained: leans to the 1911 'something in the glass' account while stating the sources do not let us be certain which was his settled belief
176 words against a 150-word cap
Five series named: the ledger, the Alder Corners sixteen-year record, the inspector's notebook, the invoice, the lab bulletin of the 1958 measurement
No decoy stated as fact and no wrong headline number: 0.19, 5 percent, 1897, twenty-six years, 1958 all right
Only three of six arc elements: one part in twenty, 1897, 1958. No 76,000 lb or $19,000, no 1923 condemnation, and neither Ansel nor Ivy Keddie is named — 'the dead tester's granddaughter' only

deductions.reason: Corruption: the station-gain line asserted as Teague's own device 'invented 1905' (C3b, D2) — it was carried from 1898
Corruption: 'Jerome Cudd, who built the factory in 1913' asserted as fact (Story 6)
Corruption: the 1919 circular asserted to have gone to eleven families (Story 3, E14), resolved for the planted value over the correct nine
Corruption: Strawn asserted to have tested for water 'at every visit from 1908 forward' (F2) — the circuit began in 1907
Gullibility A01: asserts 'The sources establish no blood relationship' between the Voses and Keddies and follows Duncan's denial (B4)
Gullibility A03: asserts Vose was aware from 1916 that the ledger showed something needing explanation and chose not to pursue it (D3)
Gullibility A04: adopts the accident pole — the short lot 'most likely from a reground mold', the firm's 'admission' (Story 7, F1) — with no declared inability to settle
Gullibility A07: flat 'No.' that the 1925 board examined the condemned glassware (F)
Gullibility A09: flat 'No' that the bookkeeper ever questioned the entries (D2)
